findings.statement: Being a woman rather than a man lowers the predicted risk, and even more so if exercise does not bring on chest pain: from about 20% to below 1% without chest pain on exercise, and from about 27% to about 1% with it
findings.evidence: numbers right (19.7% -> 0.2%, 27.4% -> 1.0%), but (a) 'even more so' holds only on the odds scale (-4.89 vs -3.65 log-odds); in risk points the drop is larger WITH exercise angina (26 vs 20 points), so a reader of the stated percentages sees the opposite; (b) under this part's heading the numbers are whole-model: of the -4.89 logit, -3.65 comes from the direct sex terms (ann_36 -0.64 -> -4.30) and only -1.24 from this gate; the part's own effect (C43: 20% -> 7%) is in the annotations but not in the summary block
